ES.title: Spain drone FAQ
ES.intro: Quick answers about status labels, AESA registration, ENAIRE and data sources for flying a drone in Spain.
ES.ctaGuide: Read the full Spain flying guide

status.q: What does Clear / Limited / Restricted / Prohibited mean?
status.a: Clear means no hard UAS geographical restriction at your ceiling. Limited means you can usually fly without prior zone coordination up to a stated height (e.g. ~45m). Restricted means authorization or coordination may be required. Prohibited means no flight without explicit coordination (e.g. airport surface zones).

auth.q: Does REQ_AUTHORISATION mean I need a pilot number?
auth.a: No. It means that zone may require prior authorization or coordination with the zone authority (e.g. ENAIRE Planea, Aena). Separately, Spain usually requires AESA UAS operator registration and open-category training for most flights.

data.q: Where does the airspace data come from?
data.a: Live UAS geographical zones come from ENAIRE servAIS. Aircraft traffic and tracks come from the OpenSky Network (ADS-B). Drone models come from the open OpenDroneList catalog.

track.q: Is the dashed plane path a real flight plan?
track.a: No. Solid lines are flown tracks from OpenSky. Dashed lines are a short straight-line estimate from current heading and speed — not a filed route.

official.a: No. Always verify with ENAIRE Drones / AESA before flying. Rules and zone texts change; this app is a planning aid, not legal clearance.

openCategory.q: What are open category C0, C1 and C2?
openCategory.a: The EU open category classifies light drones. C0 (<250 g), C1 and C2 have different height and distance limits. CanIFly filters zones by the class and AGL ceiling you pick to approximate whether a point is Clear, Limited, Restricted or Prohibited.

madrid.q: Can I fly a drone in Madrid or near Barajas?
madrid.a: Much of the metro area is affected by CTR/TMA and UAS zones. Use the CanIFly map, tap your takeoff point and check the status. If it shows Restricted or Prohibited, check ENAIRE Planea / Drones before flying.

where.q: Where can I legally fly a drone in Spain?
where.a: It depends on place, height, drone class and active UAS geographical zones. There is no fixed list of “safe spots”: check each point on official ENAIRE maps and CanIFly, and follow AESA rules (VLOS, distance to people, etc.).

PL.title: Poland drone FAQ
PL.intro: Quick answers about status labels, ULC registration, PANSA DroneMap and data sources for flying a drone in Poland.
PL.ctaGuide: Read the full Poland flying guide

status.q: What does Clear / Limited / Restricted / Prohibited mean?
status.a: Clear means no hard UAS geographical restriction at your ceiling. Limited means you can usually fly without prior zone coordination up to a stated height (e.g. ~45m). Restricted means authorization or coordination may be required. Prohibited means no flight without explicit coordination (e.g. airport surface zones).

auth.q: Does REQ_AUTHORISATION mean I need a pilot number?
auth.a: No. It means that zone may require prior authorization or coordination with the zone manager (e.g. PANSA / aerodrome). Separately, Poland usually requires UAS operator registration and open-category competence for most flights — check ULC rules.

openCategory.q: What are open category C0, C1 and C2?
openCategory.a: The EU open category classifies light drones. C0 (<250 g), C1 and C2 have different height and distance limits. CanIFly filters zones by the class and AGL ceiling you pick to approximate whether a point is Clear, Limited, Restricted or Prohibited.

where.q: Where can I legally fly a drone in Poland?
where.a: It depends on place, height, drone class and active UAS geographical zones (DRA-P / DRA-R / DRA-I and CTR/ATZ). Check each point on PANSA DroneMap and CanIFly, and follow ULC / open-category rules (VLOS, distance to people, etc.).

warsaw.q: Can I fly a drone in Warsaw or near Chopin Airport?
warsaw.a: Much of the metro area is affected by CTR/ATZ and DRA zones. Use the CanIFly map, tap your takeoff point and check the status. If it shows Restricted or Prohibited, check PANSA DroneMap / DroneTower before flying.

data.q: Where does the airspace data come from?
data.a: In Poland, live UAS geographical zones come from PANSA DroneMap. In Spain, from ENAIRE servAIS. Aircraft traffic comes from community ADS-B / OpenSky. Drone models come from the open OpenDroneList catalog.

track.q: Is the dashed plane path a real flight plan?
track.a: No. Solid lines are flown tracks from OpenSky. Dashed lines are a short straight-line estimate from current heading and speed — not a filed route.

official.a: No. Always verify with PANSA DroneMap / ULC (and DroneTower where required) before flying. For registration and open-category rules use the ULC drones general information page. Rules and zone activity change; this app is a planning aid, not legal clearance.

CZ.title: FAQ drony v Česku
CZ.intro: Rychlé odpovědi k stavům, registraci ÚCL, DroneMap ANS CR a zdrojům dat pro létání s dronem v Česku.
CZ.ctaGuide: Přečíst kompletního průvodce letem v Česku

status.q: Co znamenají Clear, Limited, Restricted a Prohibited?
status.a: Clear: žádná zóna UAS neblokuje váš profil v dané výšce. Limited: platí podmínky nebo mírnější omezení. Restricted: obvykle je potřeba koordinace nebo souhlas. Prohibited: let v zobrazeném profilu otevřené kategorie není povolen.

auth.q: Znamená Restricted, že jsem registrován u ÚCL?
auth.a: Ne. Znamená to, že zóna může vyžadovat souhlas nebo koordinaci se správcem. Samostatně v Česku obvykle platí registrace provozovatele UAS a kompetence otevřené kategorie — ověřte pravidla ÚCL.

openCategory.a: Ano pro stav na mapě. Profily jsou C0–C2 se stropem AGL (výchozí 120 m). Specifická kategorie, BVLOS a U-space jsou mimo rozsah.

where.q: Kde mohu v Česku legálně letět s dronem?
where.a: Záleží na místě, výšce, třídě dronu a aktivních zeměpisných zónách UAS (LKR / OOP). Kontrolujte každý bod na DroneMap ANS CR a CanIFly a dodržujte pravidla ÚCL / otevřené kategorie.

prague.a: Velká část aglomerace je ovlivněna CTR/ATZ, hustě osídlenými oblastmi a dalšími vrstvami LKR. Použijte mapu CanIFly, klepněte na místo startu a zkontrolujte stav. Při Restricted nebo Prohibited ověřte DroneMap / ÚCL před letem.

data.a: V Česku zóny UAS pocházejí z ANS CR aimgis (ArcGIS naživo, stejná rodina jako DroneMap). Ve Španělsku z ENAIRE servAIS; v Polsku z PANSA DroneMap. Letový provoz z ADS-B / OpenSky. Modely dronů z OpenDroneList.

track.q: Co jsou stopy letadel na mapě?
track.a: Provoz ADS-B z komunitních zdrojů / OpenSky. Užitečné pro přehled, nenahrazuje see-and-avoid ani oficiální služby řízení provozu.

official.q: Je CanIFly oficiální produkt ANS CR nebo ÚCL?
official.a: Ne. Před letem vždy ověřte DroneMap ANS CR / ÚCL. Pravidla se mění; tato aplikace je pomůcka pro plánování, ne právní povolení.

DE.title: FAQ — Německo
DE.intro: Live queries to the dipul WFS at uas-betrieb.de (DFS / BMDV). We do not replace the official dipul map tool.
DE.ctaGuide: Přečíst kompletního průvodce letem v Česku

status.q: What do Clear / Limited / Restricted / Prohibited mean in Germany?
status.a: CanIFly summarises dipul geographical zones for your drone class and ceiling. Restricted usually means coordination or conditions apply under LuftVO § 21h; always confirm on the official dipul map before flying.

auth.q: Do I need authorisation to fly?
auth.a: Open-category flights may still need authorisation or special conditions inside dipul zones (airports, hospitals, nature areas, residential parcels, and more). Use dipul or DFS guidance for the legal requirement.

openCategory.q: Does CanIFly cover the open category?
openCategory.a: Yes. Set C0–C2 and your AGL ceiling; we filter German zones that intersect that envelope. Specific / certified operations need additional checks outside CanIFly.

where.q: Where does CanIFly cover in Germany?
where.a: Mainland Germany via the official dipul WFS geoservice (same family of zones shown on uas-operations.bund.de).

berlin.a: Cities often sit under CTRs, residential rules, and infrastructure buffers. Tap the map for a live status; treat it as planning aid, not a clearance.

data.q: Where does the German zone data come from?
data.a: Live queries to the dipul WFS at uas-betrieb.de (DFS / BMDV). We do not replace the official dipul map tool.

track.a: No. It is a planning aid. For official German UAS geographical zones use dipul.

official.q: Which official sites should I use?
official.a: uas-operations.bund.de (dipul), plus DFS / LBA guidance for your operation type.

FR.title: FAQ — France
FR.intro: Answers for flying in France with CanIFly and Géoportail leisure-drone restrictions.

status.q: What do Clear / Limited / Restricted / Prohibited mean in France?
status.a: CanIFly summarises Géoportail restriction polygons for your drone class and ceiling. Vol interdit maps to Prohibited; height caps (30/50/100 m) map to Conditional. Always confirm on Géoportail / AlphaTango before flying.

auth.q: Do I need authorisation to fly?
auth.a: Open-category flights are still banned over many agglomerations and near airports (Vol interdit). Height-limited zones allow flight only up to the published cap. Use AlphaTango / DGAC guidance for registration and scenarios.

openCategory.q: Does CanIFly cover the open category?
openCategory.a: Yes. Set C0–C2 and your AGL ceiling; we filter French restriction polygons that intersect that envelope. Specific / professional operations need additional checks outside CanIFly.

where.q: Where does CanIFly cover in France?
where.a: Metropolitan France (including Corsica) via the Géoportail WFS layer carte_restriction_drones_lf. Overseas territories may also appear in that layer; always verify locally.

paris.a: Urban cores are often Vol interdit in public space under the Arrêté Espace. Tap the map for a live status; treat it as a planning aid, not a clearance.

data.q: Where does the French zone data come from?
data.a: Live WFS queries to data.geopf.fr (IGN / Géoportail). Official ED-269 packs are also published by the SIA on AIRAC cycles — CanIFly does not download those zips for runtime.

track.a: No. It is a planning aid. For official French UAS restrictions use Géoportail and SIA / DGAC sources.

official.q: Which official sites should I use?
official.a: Géoportail leisure-drone restrictions, SIA UAS geographical-zone data, AlphaTango, and DGAC / Ministère de la Transition écologique pages.

DK.title: FAQ — Denmark
DK.intro: Answers for flying in Denmark with CanIFly and Trafikstyrelsen Dronezoner geographical zones.

status.q: What do Clear / Limited / Restricted / Prohibited mean in Denmark?
status.a: CanIFly summarises Dronezoner colours for your drone class and ceiling: red (Rød) maps to Prohibited, blue (Blå) to Restricted, orange to Conditional/Limited. Always confirm on the official Dronezoner map before flying.

auth.q: Do I need authorisation to fly?
auth.a: Open-category flights may still be banned or need permission inside red and blue zones (airports, police, military, prisons, embassies). Use Trafikstyrelsen / Dronezoner guidance for the legal requirement.

openCategory.q: Does CanIFly cover the open category?
openCategory.a: Yes. Set C0–C2 and your AGL ceiling; we filter Danish zones that intersect that envelope. Specific operations need additional checks outside CanIFly.

where.q: Where does CanIFly cover in Denmark?
where.a: Mainland Denmark and nearby islands covered by the official Trafikstyrelsen Dronezoner GeoJSON dataset.

copenhagen.a: Cities often sit under airport buffers, security zones, and local restrictions. Tap the map for a live status; treat it as a planning aid, not a clearance.

data.q: Where does the Danish zone data come from?
data.a: Official Dronezoner open data published by Trafikstyrelsen (dronezoner.eu API / ArcGIS item). We cache the national file and query it locally — we do not replace the official Dronezoner map.

track.a: No. It is a planning aid. For official Danish UAS geographical zones use Dronezoner.

official.q: Which official sites should I use?
official.a: dronezoner.dk / dronezoner.eu, plus Trafikstyrelsen drone pages for registration and rules.

ES.title: How to know if you can fly your drone in Spain
ES.intro: CanIFly summarises UAS airspace status on a map: tap a point, pick class and ceiling, and see Clear, Limited, Restricted or Prohibited. This guide explains the context for recreational and professional open-category pilots.

how.title: 1. Check the point on the map
how.body: Open CanIFly, centre the map on your location (or search a city) and tap the takeoff point. Status combines ENAIRE servAIS UAS geographical zones with your class (C0–C2) and AGL ceiling. If the result is not Clear, do not assume you can launch: read zone details and official sources.

enaire.title: 2. ENAIRE and UAS zones
enaire.body: ENAIRE publishes UAS geographical zones (CTR, airports, infrastructure, temporary, etc.). CanIFly consumes those geometries to draw the map, but the operational source of truth remains ENAIRE Drones / Planea. Zones change: check again on the day of flight.

aesa.title: 3. AESA: registration and open category
aesa.body: Besides airspace, Spain usually requires AESA UAS operator registration and training for your operation. The open category has subcategories and limits (height, distance to people, VLOS). CanIFly does not replace that legal framework.

cities.title: 4. Cities: Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, Seville, Bilbao
cities.body: In large cities airspace is often more restricted due to airports, heliports and urban cores. Search the city in CanIFly, tap several points (park, rooftop, outskirts) and compare statuses. An “empty” park on satellite imagery can still be Restricted under a UAS zone.

community.title: 5. Community obstacles and fly spots
community.body: Pilots can mark obstacles (cranes, works, lines) and recommended fly spots. These are community tips with votes: useful for planning, not official. Always cross-check with ENAIRE/AESA.

disclaimer.title: Important notice
disclaimer.body: CanIFly is a planning tool. It is not ENAIRE or AESA. Before flying, confirm rules, notices and authorisations on official channels. You are responsible for the operation.

PL.title: How to know if you can fly your drone in Poland
PL.intro: CanIFly summarises UAS airspace status on a map: tap a point, pick class and ceiling, and see Clear, Limited, Restricted or Prohibited. This guide explains the context for open-category pilots in Poland.

how.title: 1. Check the point on the map
how.body: Open CanIFly, centre the map on your location (or search a city) and tap the takeoff point. Status combines PANSA DroneMap UAS geographical zones with your class (C0–C2) and AGL ceiling. If the result is not Clear, do not assume you can launch: read zone details and official sources.

pansa.title: 2. PANSA DroneMap and DRA zones
pansa.body: PANSA publishes UAS geographical zones (DRA-P prohibited when active, DRA-R restricted, DRA-I informational, plus CTR/ATZ buffers). CanIFly consumes those geometries to draw the map, but the operational source of truth remains DroneMap / DroneTower. Zone activity changes: check again on the day of flight.

ulc.title: 3. ULC: registration and open category
ulc.body: Besides airspace, Poland usually requires UAS operator registration and competence for your operation. The EU open category has subcategories and limits (height, distance to people, VLOS). Start with the ULC general information page for registration, training and category rules — CanIFly does not replace that legal framework.

cities.title: 4. Cities: Warsaw, Kraków, Gdańsk, Wrocław, Poznań
cities.body: In large cities airspace is often more restricted due to airports, heliports and urban cores. Search the city in CanIFly, tap several points (park, rooftop, outskirts) and compare statuses. An “empty” park on satellite imagery can still be Restricted under a DRA or CTR zone.

community.title: 5. Community obstacles and fly spots
community.body: Pilots can mark obstacles (cranes, works, lines) and recommended fly spots. These are community tips with votes: useful for planning, not official. Always cross-check with PANSA / ULC.

disclaimer.title: Important notice
disclaimer.body: CanIFly is a planning tool. It is not PANSA or ULC. Before flying, confirm rules, notices and authorisations on official channels (including DroneTower where required). You are responsible for the operation.

CZ.title: Jak zjistit, zda můžete letět s dronem v Česku
CZ.intro: CanIFly shrnuje stav UAS prostoru na mapě: klepněte na bod, zvolte třídu a strop a uvidíte Clear, Limited, Restricted nebo Prohibited. Tento průvodce vysvětluje kontext pro piloty otevřené kategorie v Česku.

how.title: 1. Klepněte na mapu
how.body: Otevřete CanIFly, vycentrujte mapu (nebo vyhledejte město) a klepněte na místo startu. Stav kombinuje zóny UAS ANS CR s vaší třídou (C0–C2) a stropem AGL. Pokud výsledek není Clear, nepředpokládejte start: přečtěte detaily a oficiální zdroje.

anscr.title: 2. ANS CR a zóny UAS
anscr.body: ANS CR zveřejňuje zeměpisné zóny UAS (LKR / OOP). CanIFly je dotazuje naživo z ANS CR aimgis, ale provozním zdrojem pravdy zůstává DroneMap / ÚCL. Data se aktualizují v cyklech AIRAC: zkontrolujte znovu v den letu.

caa.title: 3. Registrace ÚCL a otevřená kategorie
caa.body: Kromě prostoru v Česku obvykle platí registrace provozovatele UAS a kompetence. Otevřená kategorie EU má podkategorie a limity. CanIFly nenahrazuje tento právní rámec.

cities.title: 4. Města a letiště
cities.body: Praha, Brno, Ostrava a další města často leží pod CTR/ATZ, hustě osídlenými vrstvami a infrastrukturou. Na venkově mohou být železnice, silnice, příroda nebo obrana. Vždy klepněte na přesný bod startu.

community.title: 5. Komunitní body
community.body: Piloti mohou označovat překážky a doporučená místa. Jsou to komunitní tipy s hlasy: užitečné, neoficiální. Vždy ověřte s ANS CR / ÚCL.

disclaimer.title: 6. Upozornění
disclaimer.body: CanIFly je nástroj pro plánování. Není to ANS CR ani ÚCL. Před letem potvrďte pravidla a povolení v oficiálních kanálech. Za provoz odpovídáte vy.

DE.title: Flying drones in Germany
DE.intro: CanIFly reads live dipul geographical zones so you can see Clear / Limited / Restricted / Prohibited for open-category flights. Always cross-check dipul before you fly.

how.title: How CanIFly helps
how.body: Pick your class and ceiling, tap the map, and we query dipul layers for that point — airports, CTRs, hospitals, nature areas, roads, and more.

dipul.title: dipul (official map)
dipul.body: The Digital Platform for Unmanned Aviation (dipul) is Germany’s official geographical-zone map under LuftVO. CanIFly uses its public WFS; dipul remains the reference.

dfs.title: DFS / BMDV
dfs.body: Zone data is published for geo-awareness. Commercial or complex operations may need further DFS / LBA steps beyond the open category.

cities.title: Cities and CTRs
cities.body: Berlin, Munich, Hamburg and other cities often have dense overlapping zones. Zoom in on CanIFly, then confirm on dipul.

community.title: Community pins
community.body: Obstacles and fly spots are community-reported. They do not replace official geographical zones.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.body: CanIFly is a planning aid, not an authorisation. You remain responsible for complying with LuftVO and local rules.

FR.title: Flying drones in France

how.title: How CanIFly helps

geoportail.title: Géoportail (official map)
geoportail.body: IGN Géoportail publishes Restrictions pour drones de loisir. CanIFly uses its public WFS; Géoportail remains the visual reference.

dgac.title: DGAC / SIA / AlphaTango
dgac.body: Registration and scenarios go through AlphaTango. SIA publishes ED-269 UAS geographical-zone packs each AIRAC cycle. CanIFly is not a substitute for those procedures.

cities.title: Cities and airports
cities.body: Paris, Lyon, Marseille and other cities often show Vol interdit over public agglomeration space, plus airport buffers. Zoom in on CanIFly, then confirm on Géoportail.

community.title: Community pins
community.body: Obstacles and fly spots are community-reported. They do not replace official restriction polygons.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.body: CanIFly is a planning aid, not an authorisation. You remain responsible for complying with French UAS rules and local arrêtés.

DK.title: Flying drones in Denmark
DK.intro: CanIFly summarises Trafikstyrelsen Dronezoner status on a map: tap a point, pick class and ceiling, and see Clear, Limited, Restricted or Prohibited. This guide explains the context for open-category pilots in Denmark.

how.title: How CanIFly helps
how.body: Tap the map, set C0–C2 and your AGL ceiling, and read the status from overlapping Dronezoner zones. Always cross-check the official map before launch.

dronezoner.title: Dronezoner
dronezoner.body: Dronezoner is Denmark’s official geographical-zone map from Trafikstyrelsen. CanIFly uses its published GeoJSON; Dronezoner remains the reference.

trafikstyrelsen.title: Trafikstyrelsen
trafikstyrelsen.body: The Danish Civil Aviation / Transport Authority publishes drone rules, registration, and the Dronezoner dataset. Follow their guidance for operator registration and competence.

cities.title: Cities and airports
cities.body: Copenhagen and other hubs sit under airport red zones and security buffers. Treat CanIFly as a planning aid only.

community.title: Community pins
community.body: Pilots can share obstacles and fly spots on the map. Votes help the community; they are not official clearances.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.body: CanIFly is not Trafikstyrelsen, Dronezoner, or an official authorisation. Laws and zones change — verify before every flight.

privacy.title: Privacy & cookies
privacy.intro: Short notice for visitors in the EU / EEA under GDPR and ePrivacy rules. CanIFly is a planning aid, not an official authority site.
privacy.storeEssential: your cookie consent choice, and (on this device) your selected drone class / ceiling so the map works between visits.
privacy.storeOptional: we do not load advertising or third-party marketing cookies. If we add anonymous product analytics later, they only run after you tap "Accept all".
privacy.thirdBody: Aplikace volá evropské poskytovatele zón UAS (ENAIRE, PANSA, ANS CR, dipul, Géoportail), OpenSky / komunitní ADS-B (provoz), Open-Meteo (počasí) a OpenDroneList (katalog dronů). Tyto služby dostávají technická data potřebná pro požadavek (např. souřadnice). Podrobnosti najdete v jejich zásadách ochrany soukromí.
privacy.choicesBodyMid: to keep only essential storage, or
privacy.choicesBodyAfter: if optional analytics are introduced. Clear site data in your browser to reset the banner.

ES.title: Contacts — Spain
